title: Strict Sobolev loss and compact solvability
source_hypothesis: Explicit SL1: for a compact neighborhood A0, every supported adjoint distribution with H^r output has H^(r+m-1-epsilon) regularity for every positive epsilon. This is an assumption; its geometric proof remains open.
completed_component_scope: A regularity statement about compactly supported adjoint distributions can yield solutions near a compact set. When regularity is stated as a Sobolev index, its endpoint need not be attained. We retain that distinction throughout the duality argument. We also construct one smooth solution for smooth data by a convergent correction in every smooth seminorm.
reviewed_arguments: Escape regularity proves the adjoint gain assumed here from condition (P) and the full two-ended escape geometry. The trapping criterion gives the equivalent characteristic formulation. The finite Sobolev loss remains strict, and the smooth argument constructs one solution.

The exact two-ended escape condition persists on a compact neighborhood. The proof uses a finite unit-cotangent cover, actual nearby finite-time flows, open noncharacteristic endpoints and endpoint-base closures disjoint from K. It does not assume the trapped-leaf equivalence.

A pointwise Sobolev-index lower bound yields actual fixed-support norms only strictly below the threshold. A fixed-order finite cover and full Fourier reconstruction retain this distinction. Smoothness uses all finite global norms on the compact support.
The graph domain is complete in the original norms. Its lower output order is r-2-epsilon. The closed-graph estimate recovers q=r+m-1-epsilon and retains a one-lower-order compact term.

Every adjoint nullvector is smooth. Closedness in L2, the q=0 estimate and actual negative-order compact inclusion prove finite dimension. Full modulo-kernel coercivity is proved for every real q with its own orthogonal projection.

Nested compact neighborhoods and decreasing finite-dimensional nullspaces stabilize at precisely N(K). The necessary adjoint pairing is valid for arbitrary distributions because the nullvectors are compact and smooth.

For target t<s+m-1, the chosen positive loss is exactly s+m-1-t, the output measuring order is -t and the recovered test order is -s. Finite-chart conjugate Hahn-Banach and reciprocal Fourier weights produce a true global Ht solution near K.

The smooth proof uses the actual flat-jet quotient, its compact-support dual and every original smooth seminorm. It retains the fixed positive loss epsilon=1 and chooses a later quotient seminorm k>=j+2-m. The zero dual-bound case is handled separately.

Balanced-convex separation supplies a closure neighborhood for each source seminorm. An explicit all-seminorm summable correction removes that closure and yields one smooth solution. No bounded linear right inverse is claimed.

Three full solutions check fractional negative orders, a properly supported elliptic rank-one obstruction on a larger support, and smooth-series tails versus a Fourier obstruction to C1. Forty-two finite checks support only their stated exact algebraic identities.
